item.title: China mocks US ‘congratulations’ over Dominican closure of Chinese-run factory
item.description: China’s embassy in Santo Domingo accused the United States on Monday evening of “sinister intentions” and mocked Washington for “congratulating” the Dominican Republic on closing a Chinese-run cardboard factory. The rebuke came hours after Juan Pablo Segura, who leads the US State Department’s Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs, praised Dominican authorities on social media for “taking decisive action to shut down a massive, illegal, Chinese-operated cardboard factory”. item.title: US judge jails Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, after he cuts off his ankle monitor
item.description: The 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, was ordered to jail on Tuesday because he removed an electronic monitoring device from his ankle, just days after he was charged with possession of child sexual abuse material. item.title: Jim Jordan elected US House Republican leader after crushing midterm defeat
item.description: US House Republicans on Tuesday elected the congressman Jim Jordan as their new leader, turning to an outspoken conservative to steer the party after a crushing midterm defeat that handed Democrats control of the chamber. Jordan, 62, defeated outgoing House Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a contest that pitted calls for a fresh start against arguments for retaining experienced leadership. item.title: Canada’s Carney to raise election meddling concerns in talks with China’s Xi
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday that he would stress the importance of “non-interference in our affairs by China” when he meets President Xi Jinping later this month. A 2025 public inquiry into allegations of election meddling identified China as “the most active perpetrator of foreign interference targeting Canada’s democratic institutions”.
